# Quizlet Gravity

> Find and import Quizlet sets, create your own flashcards, and share a set link. Play as a guest or sign in and compete on each set’s high-score leaderboard.

Quizlet Gravity is Marko Sarafijanovic’s independent Gravity study game. Players type flashcard answers to defend a planet from falling asteroids. It is not affiliated with Quizlet.

## Key facts

- Website: https://www.quizletgravity.com
- Platforms: desktop and mobile browsers, Android and iOS apps
- Price: free
- Start screen: Sets, with search by set title or original Quizlet set creator
- Create sets: paste term/definition pairs or upload a CSV, with at least two pairs
- Import: public Quizlet set links, including surrounding text copied by the Quizlet app
- Sharing: public set links with a numeric ID and title slug ending in flash-cards
- Duplicate Quizlet imports: the same Quizlet set ID reuses one shared set and leaderboard
- Identity: named guests, email/password accounts with email verification, or Google sign-in
- Recovery: email recovery links for password accounts
- Leaderboards: one highest completed-game score per player per shared set, displaying level and difficulty
- Score submission: play from the shared set page and reach game over; abandoned runs and local custom games do not submit a completed score to that shared leaderboard
- Difficulties: Sloth, Easy, Medium, Hard, Mad Max
- Public data: imported/shared sets, terms, titles, creator attribution, leaderboard usernames and scores
- Private data: account emails and passwords are never shown publicly
- Local data: unshared pasted/CSV terms and theme preferences stay on the device
- Guest access: tied to the current browser or app session; registered accounts support signing in across devices
- Themes: light and dark
- Author: Marko Sarafijanovic (markosaraf)

## FAQ

### What is Quizlet Gravity?

A free flashcard game: type answers to stop asteroids from hitting your planet. Find study sets, share your own and compete with friends. This independent project is not affiliated with Quizlet.

### How do I find a study set?

Open Sets and search by title or original Quizlet set creator. Select a set to play or view its leaderboard.

### How do I import a Quizlet set?

Paste a public Quizlet set link into Import a Quizlet set, then select Import set. The full sharing text copied from the Quizlet app works too.

### How do I create my own set?

Open Create set. Enter terms and definitions, one pair per line, or upload a CSV. Check your entries before playing. You need at least two pairs.

### How do I edit an existing Quizlet set?

Open Create set → Edit a Quizlet set. Import its link, then change the terms or definitions. Your shared version credits both you and the original creator.

### How do I share a set with friends?

Open a shared set and select Copy set link. For your own set, add a title and select Create shared link first.

### Do I need an account?

No. Choose a guest username to play, import and share sets. Create an account to keep your scores across devices.

### What is the difference between a guest and an account?

A guest can lose access to their scores if app or browser data is cleared. An account lets you sign back in on any device.

### How do I confirm my email or reset my password?

Open the confirmation email after signing up. Check spam or select Resend confirmation if needed. To reset your password, select Forgot password? on the sign-in screen.

### When does my score appear on the leaderboard?

Choose Play this set on a shared set. When a red asteroid hits your planet and the game ends, your score is saved. Only your highest score for that set appears.

### How do I earn points?

Answer correctly to earn points. Keep a streak going to earn more. Wrong answers cost 10 points.

### What happens when I miss an asteroid?

Type the displayed answer to continue. Miss the same term again and the game ends. Choose an easier difficulty if you need more time.

### Can I play on my phone or tablet?

Yes, in your browser or the Android and iOS apps. Sign in with the same account to keep your scores across devices.

### Can accounts or shared sets be removed?

Accounts or sets may be removed for spam or abusive content. Removed accounts appear as Deleted user on leaderboards. Removing a set also removes its leaderboard.

### What information is public?

Shared sets, creator usernames and leaderboard scores are public. Your email and password are never shown publicly. Your own unshared sets stay on your device.
